item.title: Spain begins three days of mourning after train crash kills 69
item.description:
Emergency services, drones and dog unit continue to comb carriages as Civil Guard sets up clinics for relatives to provide DNA samples Spain has begun three days of mourning to commemorate the 69 people who died in a high-speed rail collision as hospitals continue to treat dozens of injured passengers and relatives wait for news of their loved ones. The trains – one from Spain’s state-owned Renfe and the other from the private rail company Iryo – were heading from Madrid on Wednesday to the southern region of Andalucía on the same line when they collided just before 9am. After the Iryo train came to a halt, the other slammed into its rear, knocking several carriages off the track near the town of Urda in the central region of Castilla-La Mancha. Continue reading...

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro denies fleeing Brazil after landing in Miami
item.description:
Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro, who lost Brazil's presidential election to leftist incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva on Sunday, declared himself the country's leader after arriving in Florida on Wednesday. Bolsonaro fled his country after Brazilian Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes ordered his passports to be seized less than a day after Lula won the election. "I want to say, not only to my 60 million voters but to the Brazilian people, that I am the leader and that the criminals who stole Brazil’s election are part of a criminal organization that has established a tyranny," he said in an open letter posted on X. According to Reuters, Bolsonaro initially declared himself "the elected president" in a since-deleted post. item.title: King Charles on Caribbean tour as calls grow for slavery reparations
item.description:
Britain's King Charles III chats with Governor General of the Bahamas Cynthia Pratt in Nassau, Bahamas, on Oct. 27, 2026. AP Photo/Tim Aylen King Charles III touched down in the Bahamas on Oct. 27, 2026, with far more baggage than usual. The nine-day trip in the Caribbean also features stops for the U.K. monarch in Guyana and in Antigua and Barbuda for the annual Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting. The king’s royal tour comes amid mounting Caribbean demands for reparations and renewed scrutiny of the British monarchy’s historical role in slavery . These developments have intensified debate in Caribbean Commonwealth realms over whether to retain the British monarch as head of state. item.title: Dolores Huerta – a life in pictures
item.description:
Communities across the country are grieving the death of Dolores Huerta, the renowned labor and feminist activist who empowered California’s immigrant workers. Huerta died Wednesday at the age of 96. Best known for her work advocating for farmworker rights, Huerta co-founded with Cesar Chávez in 1962 the organization that would eventually become the United Farm Workers, and organized protests and walkouts pushing for laws and labor practices to protect the immigrant communities who worked in the fields, including winning them the right to organize unions in California. Following the 1965 Delano grape strike, Huerta led a successful national boycott of table grapes that resulted in better wages and working conditions for grape pickers. She also is widely credited with conceiving and popularizing “¡Sí se puede!”— Yes we can!— a chant that still reverberates across protests and picket…

item.title: Putin seeks to expand ties with African countries at Russia-Africa summit
item.description:
Russian President Vladimir Putin’s efforts to expand his country’s influence in Africa, where China and the US have been vying for power, appear to be falling short. Though the Kremlin agreed to several deals at a summit with African leaders in Moscow — including selling fighter jets to Ethiopia and creating a geological map of Mali — barely 20 leaders attended the meeting out of more than 50 sub-Saharan nations, a sign of how Moscow’s forced recruitment of Africans to fight in its war against Ukraine has damaged its reputation. Failed defense partnerships with countries in the Sahel have also weakened its regional standing. “Public sentiment toward Russia has begun to sour across many African countries, ” Foreign Policy wrote. — Jeronimo Gonzalez

Sources: Deutsche Welle, France 24, Semafor

item.title: I’ve mailed off my vote in the US midterms. It will be a nail-biting watch, but easier from outside Trump’s America | Eleanor Limprecht
item.description:
At a campaign rally on Tuesday, President Donald Trump said his administration is going to dismantle restrictions on methane , one of the most common and potent planet-warming greenhouse gases . The new rule, proposed by the Environmental Protection Agency in response to complaints from the oil and gas industry, revises a Biden-era rule targeting methane leaks and would relax methane monitoring and emission-control requirements. The agency has planned to repeal these rules for months, saying that they posed a “monumental threat” to the economy and an “undue burden” on the oil and gas industry. item.title: Head of California high-speed rail agency resigns amid travel expenses scandal
item.description:
In summary Ian Choudri, who has led the train agency since 2024, leaves a troublesome legacy marked by budget woes, project delays and various scandals, including questionable taxpayer-funded trips by consultants. The CEO of California’s high-speed rail authority resigned late Wednesday, saying he needs to focus on “important personal and family priorities,” according to a copy of the emailed resignation obtained by CalMatters. “This has not been an easy decision, as leading the Authority has been one of the most meaningful and rewarding chapters of my professional life,” wrote Chief Executive Ian Choudri. The abrupt announcement comes in the midst of a two-day meeting of the board that oversees the project, which continues Thursday. It follows Choudri’s tumultuous two-year tenure, which has been troubled by budget woes, project delays, transparency concerns and various scandals…
